To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the psychological needs of competence, autonomy, relatedness are essential for psychological health and well being.

the satisfaction of the basic psychological needs for competence, autonomy, or relatedness yields enhanced intrinsic motivation, internalization of values, self regulation, feelings of well being, and performance; the frustration of these basic psychological needs yields diminished intrinsic motivation, internalized values, self regulation and well being and performance.

the satisfaction of innate psychological needs is the most effective way of promoting self motivation and psychological growth and well being, and that the satisfaction of those needs can be undermined by the social context in which people develop and function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extent to which the natural tendency to develop as a self motivated and well adjusted person is supported or undermined by the social context.
the promotion of psychological well being, growth, and development through the facilitation of inherent tendencies to behave in effective and satisfying ways.
the extent to which people are the proactive authors of their own lives, and the conditions that facilitate versus undermine this natural form of self motivation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more people feel competent, autonomous, and related to others, the more they feel motivated, healthy, and happy.

self determination is the capacity to live life according to one s own values, interests, and concerns and that the satisfaction of the three basic psychological needs autonomy, competence, and relatedness is critical to the promotion and support of self determined behavior.
the satisfaction of the three innate psychological needs is both necessary and sufficient for intrinsic motivation, self integration, and well being.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the satisfaction of innate psychological needs is a necessary condition for optimal functioning and mental health.

human beings have an innate propensity to develop in the direction of psychological growth and integration, provided they are offered a context that supports the satisfaction of their innate psychological needs.

human beings have a natural propensity to grow and thrive when their innate needs for competence, autonomy, relatedness, and wellness are satisfied and to become passive and alienated when their need satisfaction is thwarted.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of an individual s motivation is a function of the quality of his or her social ecological conditions.

the quality of an individual s experience of events and activities in his or her life, as well as his or her psychological health and well being, is largely determined by the extent to which these events and activities are experienced as personally meaningful and self determined.
the satisfaction of innate psychological needs is critical to optimal functioning.
